sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Waves from prerequisite order
sections.what: Explains that the order processes can be delivered in is worked out from their prerequisites, not from a model. A wave is a delivery step of six months, which is an assumption and not a measured figure.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: a model restating dependencies gets some wrong, and a process that depends on a later wave cannot be delivered earlier.
sections.watch_out: Wave length is the second largest lever on the twelve-month benefit figure, so changing it moves benefits in and out of the window.

sections.name: waves
sections.title: Assigning each process a wave
sections.what: Gives each portfolio process the earliest wave its prerequisites allow. Prerequisites that are outside the portfolio are treated as something to build in wave one, so the processes that need them come later. It raises an error if a cycle remains.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: an earlier version dropped outside prerequisites, which produced a flat plan where everything started at once.
sections.watch_out: Outside prerequisites become wave-one nodes, so a typo in a prerequisite name creates a phantom build item that delays its dependents.

sections.name: starts_month
sections.title: Month a wave begins
sections.what: Converts a wave number into the month it starts, counting from the start of the run.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file description. The formula places wave one at month zero.
sections.watch_out: Wave numbers must start at one. A zero or negative number gives a start month before the run begins.

sections.name: wave_members
sections.title: Grouping processes by wave
sections.what: Turns a map of process to wave into a list of processes for each wave, in wave order.
sections.why: Likely reason: reports list processes wave by wave, so the grouping is done once here.
sections.watch_out: Ordering is by wave number, so a wave label stored as text would sort in the wrong order.

summary: Works out delivery waves from prerequisite links, so each process starts after the work it depends on, and converts each wave into a start month.
purpose: Sets when each process starts delivering, which decides how much of its benefit lands inside the twelve-month window.
why: Stated in the docstring: the order of delivery follows from the links, and a model restating them would get some wrong. Outside prerequisites must still hold processes back.
how: Build a graph of processes and links, adding outside prerequisites as extra nodes. Rank each node by its longest chain from a starting point. Check for links left unresolved, which would mean a cycle. Keep only the portfolio's own processes. Convert wave numbers to start months and group members by wave.
inputs: Portfolio process IDs and prerequisite links, each given as a pair of IDs.
outputs: A map of process to wave number, a start month for a wave, and the processes grouped by wave.
risks: A cycle reaching this point is an error. Wave length is an assumed number. A typo in a prerequisite name creates a phantom node that delays dependent processes.
debug: If a process lands in wave one unexpectedly, check that its links are spelled correctly. If the unresolved links error appears, look for a loop among the links. If benefit timing looks wrong, check the wave length constant.
